title: Strict quasi-isomorphism fractions force every complex to be acyclic
statement: Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let K be any integer-indexed cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If quasi-isomorphisms on the category of complexes itself, with strict chain maps, have a right calculus of fractions, then K is acyclic. In particular a nonacyclic complex obstructs this calculus; this makes no claim against the valid calculus on the homotopy category.

source.place: Tag 014D, cone of an identity and its termwise split inclusion; Tag 04VC, RMS3 cancellation.

proof.text: The cone of the identity of K is acyclic, because the identity is a quasi-isomorphism. Its canonical inclusion i from K is degreewise split monic, hence monic as a map of complexes.

The zero endomorphism s of this acyclic cone is a quasi-isomorphism. It equalizes i and zero. The RMS3 right-cancellation axiom supplies a quasi-isomorphism t from some Z to K with t followed by i equal to zero.

Since i is monic, t is zero. In every degree its induced homology map is therefore both zero and an isomorphism. The target homology is zero, so K is acyclic. The argument includes unbounded complexes and is consistent when K or the category is zero.
